input.task: What is the batch code of the Nimbus Field Notebook?

provenance:
PR #34 R3 — `DRILL_TEXT_HEAD = 1_500` was published as decided behaviour in three documents of record with no eval behind it: reverting it to 300 left all 127 cases green. The reason no existing case could catch it is that the resolver searches the DOM, not the observation, so a stub plan naming a string still resolves whether or not the planner was ever shown it — which is exactly what `planner_saw` exists to separate. Here the answer is carried by the text head alone: `BC-4471` sits in a bare `` inside a `

`, and both `paragraph` and `generic` are in `observe.SKIP_ROLES`, so it is in NO observation's element list at any budget. Measured on `deep-spec.html`: the drilled subtree's text is 592 characters and `BC-4471` is at index 585 — past 300, inside 1,500. Watched red by the mutation the finding names: with `DRILL_TEXT_HEAD = 300` this case fails on `planner_saw`, because call 2's observation no longer contains the string; restored to 1,500 it passes. The prose that pushes the batch line past 300 adds no elements, so every other M32 case's measured element positions are unmoved.

triage.note: the text half of a drill-down, which is the half that matters on a page whose content carries no addressable role — ADR-020 Consequence 2 leans on exactly this ('the text head is the only thing that still reaches past it') and until now nothing held it. It grades the DISCLOSURE, not the extraction: `expect.answer` alone would pass at either width.
